title: Want a Faster Video? Playback Speed and FPS Do Different Jobs
description: Learn why playback speed and output FPS do different jobs. Check duration, motion and sound when making a faster or slower video copy on iPhone.
direct: Change playback speed to make an action finish sooner or later. Change the frame rate when a recipient needs a different number of frames per second.
figureAlt: A toy-car timing example shows ten seconds becoming five at twice the speed.
figureCaption: AI-generated conceptual illustration, not an App screenshot or measured export. The times are a calculated uniform-speed example.
cards.decision.heading: Start with the distinction
cards.decision.body: A normal-speed conversion can drop or repeat frames while keeping the same timeline. Reinterpreting recorded frames at another rate is a different operation that can create slow motion. Decide whether you need a new pace or a delivery-rate requirement.
sections.detail-0.heading: A simple timing example
sections.detail-0.body: For a uniform 2× speed change, a ten-second action occupies five seconds. This is arithmetic, not a measured app export. By contrast, converting a ten-second clip from 60 to 30 FPS can still produce ten seconds of normal-speed action. The exact motion appearance depends on how the conversion samples frames; more FPS alone does not create a faster story.
sections.detail-1.heading: Check audio separately
sections.detail-1.body: Apple’s iMovie guide treats video speed and pitch behavior as separate choices. That does not establish a matching pitch switch in our app. No optical-flow slow-motion generation, pitch-preservation option or fixed speed range is claimed here. Re-encoding cannot reveal movement the camera never captured.
faqs.reader-question-1.heading: Will changing 60 FPS to 30 FPS make a ten-second video last twenty seconds?
faqs.reader-question-1.body: A normal-speed conversion can keep it at ten seconds. Reinterpreting the same recorded frames at a different rate is a separate operation.
faqs.reader-question-2.heading: What should I check after speeding up a talking clip?
faqs.reader-question-2.body: Listen to the voice and check that speech still lines up with the picture. Try a milder speed if the words become hard to follow.

steps.step-1.text: Keep the original and note its duration. Choose one clear goal: faster action, slower action, or the same action at a requested FPS.
steps.step-2.text: For an actual pace change in Phone Cleaner: Photo & Video, use the Pro video-speed tool. Select an available speed and export a separate copy.
steps.step-3.text: Check the saved duration, moving subjects and sound. Listen for voice changes and inspect synchronization before sharing. Use a milder speed if motion or speech becomes difficult to follow.
